create.title: Literal smooth residual blockwise M1 estimate
create.statement_tex: For every real X and every literal smooth physical M1 label (D,L) in U_1, prove B_1(D,L;X)<<_epsilon X^(1/4+epsilon), uniformly with the exact Vaaler taper, both frequency signs, denominator profile, height floor, endpoint stars and half weights, support crossings, and real-X boundary convention. The unique hard profile containing d=floor(sqrt X) is excluded and belongs to M9-M1-top-endpoint-signed-cone. This is a physical blockwise estimate, not a global angular-radial or conductor packet.
create.next_action: Prove the literal smooth residual estimate, or replace it and the hard child by one whole-U_1 theorem such as the exact odd-kernel or RCS target. Do not import the global canonical Gram without a block-local inverse.

create.title: Physical one-count assembly of all blockwise M1 packets
create.statement_tex: Use the exact denominator partition with one unexpanded bottom, one hard profile containing d=floor(sqrt X), and otherwise smooth profiles; the exact clipped frequency partition; and owner priority R5-Full, terminal divisor theorem, full second derivative, then TTY. The remaining main set is U_1={(delta,ell) in Omega: ell<delta-1/4, 178ell+1638delta>463} minus {(1/2,0)}. Split its literal labels by physical profile. If the middle/lower residual hard signed cone and the literal smooth residual blockwise estimate hold uniformly with every profile, floor, star, sign, support crossing, and real-X endpoint, then every M1 block is O_epsilon(X^(1/4+epsilon)); the logarithmic one-count assembly proves M9-M1.
create.next_action: Prove the two open physical parents. The one-count blockwise assembly itself is complete.

create.title: Canonical M1 Gram does not localize every physical block
create.statement_tex: The canonical hard actual-symbol Gram theorem owns only one transition-flattened smooth nonaxial principal packet in J^(13/18)<C_cond<=J^(3/4), after global angular recombination and product-wavelet/Farey refinements. That route has summed away the physical L partition and supplies no inverse localization to an individual B_1(D,L;X). Even if the Gram theorem is assumed, it controls neither the middle/lower hard top cone nor every smooth physical U_1 block and therefore does not imply blockwise M9-M1. In its global route it also leaves C_cond>J^(3/4), raw transitions, axes, cone edges, other radial sectors, and radial/top interfaces.
create.next_action: Use the canonical Gram only inside its global lower-radial conductor child. A blockwise consequence requires a new localization theorem.

create.title: Exact lower-radial signed aggregate for global M1
create.statement_tex: Fix a smooth lower cutoff in n/sqrt X, equal to one near zero and disjoint from the proved compact critical interior. For the exact C_X^*(n), prove the corresponding lower-radial sum sum_n V_low(n/sqrt X)C_X^*(n)n^(-3/4)e(sqrt(Xn))<<_epsilon X^epsilon, with all dyadic lower scales, floors, stars, signs, and hard-top incidences assembled once. On fixed blocks nu<=2/5 the target-safe one-sided divisor replacement may be used but its signed radial sum remains open; above 2/5 both the exact correction and signed limiting cone are retained.
create.next_action: Prove the exact lower-radial signed aggregate. Treat alpha and product-wavelet/conductor decompositions as alternative refinements, not simultaneous owners.

create.title: Sharp radial endpoint and interface estimate for global M1
create.statement_tex: For the exact C_X^*(n), prove the normalized X^epsilon bound for the sharp upper radial endpoint n=16sqrt X and the finite support, cutoff, and top-interface pieces excluded by the proved smooth critical transfer and the chosen lower cutoff. Retain the endpoint star, hard sample, floors, signs, and all transform boundary terms. This is a physical radial-interface owner; the connector-completed alpha branch is an alternative transformed architecture rather than an additional summand.
create.next_action: Prove the exact sharp radial/top interface package without extending the compact critical theorem to its excluded endpoint.

create.title: Coarse radial one-count assembly of global active M1
create.statement_tex: Choose one fixed smooth partition of the exact finite n<=16sqrt X sum into a lower cutoff, finitely many compact critical functions, and the sharp upper/interface remainder. The compact critical functions are proved by M9-M1-smooth-critical-radial-terminal-transfer. If the exact lower-radial signed aggregate and the sharp radial/interface estimate are O_epsilon(X^epsilon), then the full global angular-radial estimate follows. Alpha, near-product, product-wavelet, and conductor decompositions are alternative nested attacks inside unresolved children and are not additional flat owners.
create.next_action: Prove the two open radial parents. Refine a child by alpha or conductor variables only with an explicit successive-complement identity.

create.title: GAR is equivalent to the total active M1 target
create.statement_tex: The exact global recombination gives M_(1,active)^stat(X)=-(4/pi)X^(1/4)G_X+O(log^2 X), with the inactive bottom and transform errors separately O_epsilon(X^(1/4+epsilon)). Therefore M9-M1-global-angular-radial-estimate is exactly sufficient for the total active M1 contribution at the quarter scale. It does not imply any individual dyadic B_1(D,L;X) bound and hence does not imply blockwise M9-M1 or the blockwise M9 node.
create.next_action: Use this only in the alternative total-M1 Gauss-circle bridge. Do not infer blockwise M9-M1.

create.title: Alternative Gauss-circle bridge using global M1
create.statement_tex: H1-H3, H4, R5-Full, the exact GAR-to-total-active-M1 equivalence, and blockwise M9-M2 imply P(X)<<_epsilon X^(1/4+epsilon). This is an alternative to the standard blockwise M9 bridge: the global M1 estimate controls the total active M1 contribution, while M9-M2 controls every M2 block. It does not prove the blockwise M9 or M9-M1 statements.
create.next_action: Close either GAR plus M9-M2 through this route, or retain the standard blockwise M9 route. Do not conjoin the two alternatives as packet owners.
